content:
The [401(k) Calculator](/401k-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Project how your 401(k) grows — balance, contributions, employer match and returns. Enter your current 401(k) balance, your contribution per year, employer match per year, expected annual return and years until retirement and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Project what your 401(k) could be worth at retirement from your current balance, yearly contributions, employer match and an assumed annual return. The 2025 employee contribution limit is $23,500 if you are under 50, or $31,000 with the $7,500 catch-up contribution at 50 and over — employer matches do not count toward that limit. This is a projection, not a promise: real returns vary every year, and the result assumes steady end-of-year contributions and a constant return.

## How to use the 401(k) Calculator

Start by entering your current 401(k) balance, then entering your your contribution per year, entering your employer match per year, entering your expected annual return (%) and finally entering your years until retirement. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter your current 401(k) balance.
2. Enter what you contribute each year, and your employer match per year.
3. Set the annual return you expect — 7% is a common long-run planning figure.
4. Enter the years until you plan to retire and read the projected balance.

## Formula

Future value = balance × (1 + r)^n + yearly × ((1 + r)^n − 1) ÷ r, where r is the annual return and n the number of years. Yearly = your contribution + employer match.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [401(k) Calculator](/401k-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Starting with $10,000, contributing $12,000 a year with a $3,000 employer match, at a 7% annual return for 30 years, the projection is $1,493,034.35 — $450,000 of contributions plus $1,033,034.35 of growth on top of the starting balance. Try the same figures in the [401(k) Calculator](/401k-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Current 401(k) balance: 10000, Your contribution per year: 12000, Employer match per year: 3000, Expected annual return: 7 %, Years until retirement: 30), the [401(k) Calculator](/401k-calculator) returns Projected balance: $1,493,034.35, Your contributions + match: $450,000, Starting balance: $10,000, Investment growth: $1,033,034.35, 2025 contribution limit (under 50): $23,500. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## The 2025 limits

For 2025 you can contribute up to $23,500 of your own pay to a 401(k), or $31,000 if you are 50 or older thanks to the $7,500 catch-up. Employer matching contributions are extra and do not count toward your limit. The combined employee-plus-employer limit for 2025 is $70,000 ($77,500 with catch-up). If your yearly contribution above is over the limit, the projection still runs — treat the limit line as a check, not a cap.

## Why the match matters most

An employer match is an instant, guaranteed return on your contribution — a 100% match on the first 3% of pay doubles that money on day one, before any investment growth. If your plan offers a match, contributing at least enough to get the full match is almost always the best first move, because no investment reliably beats a guaranteed 100%.

## What this projection assumes

The calculation compounds once a year at a fixed rate, with contributions made at the end of each year. Real 401(k)s compound more often, returns swing up and down, fees take a small cut, and your contributions usually rise with your salary. The result is an estimate for planning — it is not financial advice and not a forecast of what you will actually have.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Always contribute at least enough to get your full employer match — it is free money.
- A 1% higher return compounds to a much larger balance over 30 years; fees matter as much as returns.
- Raise your contribution by 1% each year when you get a pay rise and you will barely feel it.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much can I contribute to a 401(k) in 2025?

$23,500 if you are under 50, or $31,000 if you are 50 or older (the extra $7,500 is the catch-up contribution). Employer matches do not count toward your limit. Try it with your own numbers in the [401(k) Calculator](/401k-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What return should I assume for a 401(k) projection?

Many planners use 6–8% a year as a long-run average for a diversified stock-heavy portfolio, before inflation. Try 5% for a cautious view and 8% for an optimistic one — the gap between them shows how much returns matter. Try it with your own numbers in the [401(k) Calculator](/401k-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is a 401(k) projection a guarantee?

No. It assumes a steady return every year, but real markets go up and down. The projection is a planning estimate, not financial advice — for decisions about your retirement savings, speak to a qualified financial adviser. Try it with your own numbers in the [401(k) Calculator](/401k-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the 401(k) Calculator use?

Future value = balance × (1 + r)^n + yearly × ((1 + r)^n − 1) ÷ r, where r is the annual return and n the number of years. Yearly = your contribution + employer match. You can see it in action in the [401(k) Calculator](/401k-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
